scope: Printed edition and apparatus at Isaiah 54:11–13; not a direct manuscript collation

source.title: Henry Barclay Swete, The Old Testament in Greek according to the Septuagint, volume III
source.method: PDF hash matched existing manifest; pypdf OCR used for navigation, complete relevant pages rendered with pdftoppm and visually inspected, target also inspected at original resolution
source.edition_date_basis: Title page PDF 7 and edition history PDF 8, not uploader metadata

main_text.text: καὶ θήσω τὰς ἐπάλξεις σου ἴασπιν καὶ τὰς πύλας σου λίθους κρυστάλλου καὶ τὸν περίβολόν σου λίθους ἐκλεκτούς
main_text.normalization: Removed printed punctuation and verse numbers, retained accents; not a diplomatic transcription of the underlying manuscript
main_text.comparison_difference: Swete prints final ἐκλεκτούς with acute; pinned Rahlfs surface field has ἐκλεκτοὺς with grave. Preserve both source forms; lexical sequence agrees, raw strings do not.

apparatus.report_policy: Preserve edition hand labels without asserting a newly verified physical hand or chronology; crystal report carries vid and is not certain manuscript transcription
apparatus.scope_limit: Selected old uncial apparatus; absence of a report is not exhaustive modern Greek collation

conventions.locator: Introduction v–vi, PDF 9–10; sigla list PDF 24
conventions.result: Vaticanus generally supplies text/order through Prophets. B, א, A and Q identify Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Marchalianus. Book-specific bases differ elsewhere.
Marchalianus text, corrections and Hexaplaric annotations must be separated; grouped editorial notation is not an independent-witness count.

Swete explicitly warns that silence of Cryptoferratensis Γ can reflect inability to decipher. Γ is not among the target page's apparatus margin sigla; no target omission vote is assigned to it. OCR misidentifies this siglum as F.

next_full_apparatus.edition: Joseph Ziegler, Isaias, Göttingen Septuaginta XIV, third edition, 1983

assessment.decision: Retain POB Hebrew and English provisionally; bounded printed Greek corroboration, not resolution of the pesher quantifier or Hebrew lexical alternatives
assessment.counterargument: Greek absence still may reflect translation practice; the versions also omit the WLC boundary quantifier. An older selected apparatus may omit relevant later-catalogued evidence.
